questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests basic Kubernetes security and governance in a common repo layout.

## Key Concepts
- NetworkPolicy: default-deny per namespace
- securityContext: runAsNonRoot and runAsUser
- resources: requests and limits per container

## Code Example
```yaml
# Failing manifest (excerpt)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: service-a
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/app:1.0.0
        # missing securityContext and resources
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (excerpt)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: service-a
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny
  namespace: service-a
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: ["Ingress", "Egress"]
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: service-a
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 1000
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/app:1.0.0
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "250m"
            memory: "256Mi"
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt the gate for multiple clusters with different namespace policies?
- What are potential performance implications of parsing many manifests in CI?

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked
- Tests ability to translate governance requirements into concrete, enforceable policies and CI steps. 
- Combines data catalog metadata with image provenance and basic security gates in a beginner-friendly way.

Key Concepts
- Policy as code (Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper)
- Annotations for data governance (data-catalog.uri)
- Image provenance (digest pinning, registry allowlist)
- Basic hardening (forbidden hostNetwork/hostPath, non-privileged)
- Namespace quotas and network policies

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: governance-baseline
spec:
  rules:
  - name: require-data-catalog
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "data.catalog.uri annotation required"
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            data.catalog.uri: "?*"
  - name: require-image-digest
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "image must be pinned with digest"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: "*@sha256:*"
  - name: disallow-risky-fields
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod", "Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    prune: false
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork/hostPath/privileged not allowed"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: False
        volumes: []
```

Failing Manifest (example)
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: data-processor
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      hostNetwork: true
      volumes:
        - name: data
          hostPath:
            path: /data
      containers:
        - name: processor
          image: registry.internal/data-processor:latest
```

Passing Manifest (example)
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: data-processor
  namespace: team-a
  annotations:
    data.catalog.uri: "https://catalog.example.org/datasets/123"
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: processor
          image: registry.internal/data-processor@sha256:abcdef123456...
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "128Mi"
              limits:
              cpu: "200m"
              memory: "256Mi"
```

Follow-up notes
- How would you test the policy in CI (e.g., kyverno test, simulate PRs)?
- How to handle exceptions per-namespace while preserving governance?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests binding of feature flags to artifact provenance and touches CI, runtime, and security controls across tenants.

## Key Concepts
- cosign signing and repo public keys
- SBOMs (CycloneDX)
- central provenance store and attestations
- manifest digest binding to provenance
- Kyverno admission policy

## Code Example
```yaml
name: Sign-and-attest
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  build-and-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        run: docker build -t my-registry/svc:$GITHUB_SHA .
      - name: cosign sign
        run: cosign sign --key cosign.pub my-registry/svc:$GITHUB_SHA
      - name: generate SBOM
        run: cyclonedx-bom -o bom.xml my-registry/svc:$GITHUB_SHA
      - name: upload SBOM
        run: curl -X POST -F file=@bom.xml https://provenance-store.local/upload
``` 

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test cross-tenant consistency?
- How would you rotate keys without breaking in-flight deploys?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests basic security posture enforcement in manifests, a real-world gate that beginners can implement with standard policy engines.

## Key Concepts
- container securityContext: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities (drop ALL)
- privileged flag handling
- policy engines: Kyverno, OPA Gatekeeper

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno policy (minimal)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secctx
spec:
  rules:
  - name: check-security
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet", "DaemonSet", "Pod"]
    validate:
      message: "Containers must set runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and drop ALL capabilities"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ["ALL"]
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (no securityContext, privileged)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: foo
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
        securityContext:
          privileged: true
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (proper securityContext)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: bar
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:1.21
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt the gate for multi-tenant clusters with namespace-scoped policies?
- What would you test locally to avoid CI regressions?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design end-to-end software supply chain security for ML deployments, including signing, attestation, and gatekeeping at deployment time across multi-cloud teams.

## Key Concepts
- ML artifact signing with Cosign
- Rekor attestations and verification
- SBOMs for ML assets and pipelines
- Deployment gates via policy engines (OPA-like) and CI integration
- Tamper testing and revocation handling

## Code Example
```bash
# Generate signing keys (one-time)
cosign generate-key-pair

# Sign artifacts
cosign sign -key cosign.key models/weights.pt
cosign sign -key cosign.key data/config.json

# Create attestations
cosign attest -key cosign.key -predicate attestation.json models/weights.pt

# Verify artifacts
cosign verify weights.pt
cosign verify data/config.json
```

## Follow-up Questions

## Why This Question Is Asked
This tests practical policy design, edge-case handling, and CI integration for Kubernetes manifests in a multi-team environment. Candidates must demonstrate understanding of resource isolation, pod hardening, network security, and hardware scheduling constraints.

## Key Concepts
- **ResourceQuota and LimitRange**: Prevent resource starvation and enforce default resource requests/limits per namespace
- **Pod securityContext**: Enforce runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and capability dropping for workload hardening
- **Ingress TLS with cert-manager**: Ensure encrypted external traffic with automated certificate management
- **GPU scheduling constraints**: Use nodeSelector and resource requests to restrict GPU workloads to approved namespaces and nodes
- **CI validation**: Integrate Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper with kubectl dry-run for pre-merge enforcement

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy for ML Platform Gates
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-ml-platform-gates
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
    - name: require-resource-quota
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Namespace]
      validate:
        message: "Each namespace must have a ResourceQuota."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              quota-ready: "true"

    - name: require-security-context
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      validate:
        message: "Containers must run as non-root with read-only filesystem and drop ALL capabilities."
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop: [ALL]

    - name: require-ingress-tls
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Ingress]
      validate:
        message: "Ingress must use TLS with cert-manager annotation."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              (cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer): "?*"
          spec:
            tls:
              - secretName: "?*"

    - name: gpu-in-approved-namespaces
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      preconditions:
        - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
          operator: In
          value: ["1", "2", "4"]
      validate:
        message: "GPU pods are only allowed in approved namespaces with nvidia nodeSelector."
        pattern:
          spec:
            nodeSelector:
              nvidia.com/gpu: "?*"
```

## Verification Strategy

**Local Testing:**
```bash
# Install Kyverno
kubectl apply -f policy.yaml

# Dry-run validate manifests
kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f manifest.yaml

# Test policy against sample manifests
kyverno apply policy.yaml --manifest manifest.yaml
```

**CI Integration (GitHub Actions):**
```yaml
name: Manifest Validation
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate with Kyverno
        run: |
          kyverno apply cluster-policy.yaml \
            --manifest manifests/ \
            --policy-report \
            --fail-only-on-exists
```
